meta.name: Preposition Case Rules
meta.description: Rules for German prepositions: which case each governs, with notes for two-way (Wechsel) prepositions and special cases. Used by the Grammar Rules browser and the verb+preposition review hints.

categories.two-way: Wechselpräposition — spatial destination/change of location uses Akk; spatial location uses Dat; lexical combinations are learned with their case

an.rule: In spatial uses, an takes Accusative for a destination/change of location (wohin?) and Dative for location (wo?) — movement can occur with either. Lexical combinations must be learned with their case.

auf.rule: In spatial uses, auf takes Accusative for a destination/change of location (wohin?) and Dative for location (wo?) — movement can occur with either. Lexical combinations must be learned with their case.

in.rule: In spatial uses, in takes Accusative for entry into a destination (wohin?) and Dative for location within it (wo?) — movement can occur with either. Lexical combinations must be learned with their case.

über.rule: In spatial uses, über contrasts destination/change of location (Accusative) with location (Dative). In lexical combinations, learn the stored case with the whole phrase; many common combinations use Accusative (sprechen/nachdenken/sich freuen über).

unter.rule: In spatial uses, unter contrasts destination/change of location (Accusative) with location (Dative). Lexical combinations have their own case, for example leiden unter + Dative.

vor.rule: In spatial uses, vor contrasts destination/change of location (Accusative) with location (Dative). Common lexical combinations such as Angst haben, sich fürchten, and warnen vor use Dative.

zwischen.rule: In spatial uses, zwischen contrasts destination/change of location (Accusative) with location (Dative). Lexical combinations must be learned with their case; unterscheiden zwischen uses Dative.

hinter.rule: In spatial uses, hinter takes Accusative for a destination/change of location (wohin?) and Dative for location (wo?). Lexical combinations must be learned with their case.

neben.rule: In spatial uses, neben takes Accusative for a destination/change of location (wohin?) and Dative for location (wo?). Lexical combinations must be learned with their case.

als.rule: als is a comparison/predicative particle, not a case-governing preposition. With subject-related predicates (gelten/dienen/fungieren als), the complement is nominative. With object-related constructions (jemanden als etwas wahrnehmen; etwas als Leistung anrechnen), it follows the object's case. Learn the complete construction shown on the card.
